$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}{y}^{2}-x,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{5}.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $-\frac{4}{25}$ | {{field-1}} |

examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = xy^2 - x^2, \qquad y(0)=2
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $\Delta x = \dfrac12.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $2$ | $0$ | $0$ | $2$ | $\dfrac{7}{4}$ |  |
examples.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y_0 = y(x_0),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y'_p = f(x_\text{new},y_p)$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $(x_\text{new}, y_p) = (x + \Delta x, y + \Delta y_p).$

We compute $\Delta y$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0+\frac{7}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{7}{4}) \\  & =\frac{7}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,y'\,$ | $\Delta y_p$ | $y_p$ | $y'_p$ | $\Delta y$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $2$ | $0$ | $0$ | $2$ | $\dfrac{7}{4}$ | $\dfrac{7}{16}$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2y,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2},$ fill the missing entries in the table below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the predictor equation of the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p}={y}^{′}\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

The initially predicted new $y$-value is then given by ${y}_{p}=y+Δ{y}_{p}.$

First, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x+2y \\  & =0+2\cdot 1 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We add this value to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ |  |

Hence, according to the predictor equation, the initially predicted new $y$-value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p} \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |
